summary: Mr. Mosseri examines the proper berakha for eating Melabes (sugar-coated almonds) according to various communities and rabbinic sources. He discusses the custom of Baghdad recorded in Binyan Hai by Rabbi Yosef Chaim, as well as the Halabi minhag found in Peri Saddiq, the writings of Hakham Shmuel Laniado, and Royne Aman by Hakham Yitzchak Shehebar. The class explores whether one should recite Ha-Etz, Shehakol, or separate the sugar coating from the almond.

questions: What berakha is recited on Melabes according to the minhag of Halab?
How did the father of Rabbi Yosef Chaim (author of Binyan Hai) eat sugar-coated almonds?

Which Halabi books and Hakhamim address the berakha for Melabes?
